import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import odl
from odl.contrib import tomo

2D Case¶

In [49]:
# Define the 2D reconstruction space
recospace_2d = odl.uniform_discr(
    [-112, -112],
    [112, 112],
    (128, 128),
)

# Define the 2D cone beam geometry
geometry_2d = odl.tomo.cone_beam_geometry(
    space=recospace_2d,
    src_radius=780.0,
    det_radius=220.0,
    num_angles=128,
    short_scan=True,
)

# Create the 2D ray transform operator
raytrafo_2d = odl.tomo.RayTransform(
    vol_space=recospace_2d,
    geometry=geometry_2d,
)

# The 2D dataspace is the range of the operator
dataspace_2d = raytrafo_2d.range
In [50]:
# Phantom and data
phantom = odl.phantom.transmission.shepp_logan(space=recospace_2d, modified=False)
data = raytrafo_2d(phantom)

# Relative noise level
rel_level = 0.01

# Generate unit-norm white noise
noise = odl.phantom.white_noise(space=dataspace_2d, mean=0, stddev=1.0, seed=42)
noise = noise / noise.norm()

# Scale relative to data norm
noise = noise * rel_level * data.norm()

# Add to data
data_noisy = data + noise

print(noise.norm()/data.norm())

phantom.show(title="Phantom")
data.show(title="Clean data")
data_noisy.show(title="Noisy data")
plt.show()

In [ ]:
res_norm = []
error_norm = []
# for only least sq. then stability region is: 0 < alpha < 2/||A||^2
# Set as initial step length guess (larger then expected)
alpha0 = 1 / raytrafo_2d.norm(estimate=True)**2
lam = 1

for i, epsilon in enumerate(epsilon_list):
    huber_norm = odl.solvers.Huber(grad_op.range, epsilon)
    regularizer = lam * odl.solvers.functional.functional.FunctionalComp(huber_norm,grad_op)
    l2_norm = odl.solvers.L2NormSquared(dataspace_2d).translated(data_noisy)
    data_fidelity = 0.5 * odl.solvers.functional.functional.FunctionalComp(l2_norm,raytrafo_2d)
    f = data_fidelity + regularizer
    x = recospace_2d.zero()
    # line search to decide step length, estimate_step=True: use previous step as initial guess
    line_search = odl.solvers.BacktrackingLineSearch(function=f, max_num_iter=20, alpha=alpha0, tau=0.5, discount=1e-4, estimate_step=True)
    odl.solvers.smooth.gradient.steepest_descent(f,x, maxiter=150, line_search=line_search)
    
    res = (data_noisy - raytrafo_2d(x)).norm()
    res_norm.append(res)
    error = (phantom - x).norm()
    error_norm.append(error)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def compare_phantom_reco(suptitle, phantom, reco, N=50):

    # Convert to numpy arrays if needed
    phantom_arr = phantom.asarray() if hasattr(phantom, "asarray") else phantom
    reco_arr = reco.asarray() if hasattr(reco, "asarray") else reco

    # Center patch indices
    cx, cy = phantom_arr.shape[0] // 2, phantom_arr.shape[1] // 2
    phantom_patch = phantom_arr[cx-N//2:cx+N//2, cy-N//2:cy+N//2]
    reco_patch = reco_arr[cx-N//2:cx+N//2, cy-N//2:cy+N//2]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 10))
    fig.suptitle(suptitle, fontsize=14)

    # Full phantom
    im0 = axes[0, 0].imshow(phantom_arr, cmap='gray')
    axes[0, 0].set_title("Full phantom")
    plt.colorbar(im0, ax=axes[0, 0])

    # Full reconstruction
    im1 = axes[0, 1].imshow(reco_arr, cmap='gray')
    axes[0, 1].set_title("Full reconstruction")
    plt.colorbar(im1, ax=axes[0, 1])

    # Zoomed phantom
    im2 = axes[1, 0].imshow(phantom_patch, cmap='gray')
    axes[1, 0].set_title(f"Zoomed phantom ({N}x{N})")
    plt.colorbar(im2, ax=axes[1, 0])

    # Zoomed reconstruction
    im3 = axes[1, 1].imshow(reco_patch, cmap='gray')
    axes[1, 1].set_title(f"Zoomed reconstruction ({N}x{N})")
    plt.colorbar(im3, ax=axes[1, 1])

    plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])  # leave space for suptitle
    plt.show()

Plotting $\lambda$:s¶

In [33]:
def Huber_reconstruction(raytrafo_2d, 
                         x, 
                         dataspace_2d,
                         sinogram_noisy, 
                         grad_op, 
                         epsilon, 
                         lam, 
                         niter=800):
    
    alpha0 = 1 / raytrafo_2d.norm(estimate=True)**2

    huber_norm = odl.solvers.Huber(grad_op.range, epsilon)
    regularizer = lam * odl.solvers.functional.functional.FunctionalComp(huber_norm,grad_op)
    l2_norm = odl.solvers.L2NormSquared(dataspace_2d).translated(sinogram_noisy)
    data_fidelity = 0.5 * odl.solvers.functional.functional.FunctionalComp(l2_norm,raytrafo_2d)
    f = data_fidelity + regularizer
    line_search = odl.solvers.BacktrackingLineSearch(function=f, max_num_iter=20, alpha=alpha0, tau=0.5, discount=1e-4, estimate_step=True)  # Armijo rule
    odl.solvers.smooth.gradient.steepest_descent(f,x, maxiter=niter, line_search=line_search)
    
    return x
In [ ]:
lambdas = np.linspace(0.5, 10, 4)
noise_levels = np.linspace(0.8, 24, 6) / 100  # e.g. 0.8%, 1.0%, 1.2%

# unit white noise
unit_noise = odl.phantom.white_noise(space=dataspace_2d, mean=0, stddev=1.0)
unit_noise /= unit_noise.norm()

nsteps = 150
chunk = 5

for rel_level in noise_levels:
    # new figure per noise level
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))

    # scale the SAME unit noise for this noise level
    noise = unit_noise.copy() * (rel_level * data.norm())
    print(noise.norm())
    data_noisy = data + noise
    
    x = recospace_2d.zero()
    errors = []
    iters = []

    for lam in lambdas:
        # init
        x = recospace_2d.zero()
        iters = [0]
        errors = [(x - phantom).norm()]

        # run in chunks
        for k in range(0, nsteps, chunk):
            x = Huber_reconstruction(
                raytrafo_2d=raytrafo_2d,
                x=x,
                dataspace_2d=dataspace_2d,
                sinogram_noisy=data_noisy,
                grad_op=grad_op,
                epsilon=epsilon,
                lam=lam,
                niter=chunk
            )
            iters.append(k + chunk)
            errors.append((x - phantom).norm())

        ax.plot(iters, errors, marker='o', label=fr"$\lambda={lam:.2f}$")

    ax.set_title(f"rel noise = {rel_level:.2%}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Iterations")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\|x - x_{\mathrm{true}}\|$")
    ax.grid(True, which="both")
    ax.legend()

    fig.suptitle(r"Iterations vs error (Huber)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
